target_customer: Sales teams and founders who send decks, videos and PDFs to buyers and investors
problem: Static decks and scattered links give senders no view of who engaged, and buyers get a poor experience.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription (14 day trial per current site)
product_category: Interactive sales storytelling and digital sales rooms

founders.name: Peter Clark
founders.background_notes: About 15 years in B2B growth per YC profile.

technical_complexity.rationale: A no-code web page builder embedding slides, video and calendars plus view analytics; standard web engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Pages are easy to replicate, but sales content hosted and tracked in one place gives mild switching costs.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Document sharing and presentation tools expanded into similar features; the company still operates its own site, and no acquirer is named in sources.

market_need_then: Remote selling and fundraising in 2020 to 2021 increased sending of decks and links; no spend figures found.

identity.logo: New brand introduced mid 2022 (details not found)
identity.voice_and_tone: Founder blog treats brand as a practical startup lever

brand_strength.rationale: Company published posts on brand and a 2022 rebrand, but no outside coverage of brand impact; the generic name is shared with several unrelated companies.

outcome_analysis: Journey was a no-code interactive sales page tool from founders with senior growth, engineering and sales backgrounds at AdRoll, Udemy, Quora and Facebook. It raised a pre-seed led by Susa Ventures in October 2022 and YC lists it as acquired, but no acquirer or date was found, and its site still markets the product. The outcome cannot be explained beyond that, so failure factors stay empty.
notes: Seedtable lists the 2022-10 round at 4.1M and another aggregator suggests an 8M seed in 2025; both are single aggregator figures, unverified, so no amount is recorded. Other totals (4M, 7.7M) conflict. Acquirer and date not found although the site still operates. Competitor search returned only current aggregator pages, so competitors left empty.
